title: Orbit and Terminal Anew
premise: Ivo Eastwick, a xenolinguist whose mind was rewired by contact with an alien signal years ago, tends the orbital beacon above the forgotten colony of Terminal Anew. When the colony's children begin dreaming in unison—dreams that are unmistakably the beacon's voice—Ivo realizes the signal was never a greeting but a countdown, and two rival fleets are converging on the colony believing it to be a weapons test site. To save the children and the colonists, Ivo must fabricate a single convincing lie broadcast in both fleets' languages: that Terminal Anew is already dead of plague. The lie holds just long enough for the fleets to turn away, but Ivo must sacrifice their own place among humans, staying aboard the beacon as its new living voice—the ending finds them no longer dreaming in any language at all, yet finally belonging somewhere.
about_author: Vesper Sterling is the pen name of a former radio astronomer who left observatory work after claiming to have heard 'a sentence' in the noise. They now write from a decommissioned listening station on the coast, where they insist the static still talks back.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A day in the life maintaining the ancient beacon above Terminal Anew: calibrations, ration logs, and one-sided conversations with a machine that answers in fragments. Establishes Ivo's isolation and their habit of speaking aloud in languages they can't name. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness mistaken for contentment.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Night
chapters.summary: Dual POV opening on Sefa, age nine, who wakes her whole dormitory because everyone dreamed the same falling star. The colony's teacher dismisses it; the children don't. Sefa sketches the dream: a tower of light counting backward. Emotional beat: unease blooming into wonder.

chapters.title: Grammar of the Dead Signal
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo decodes a corrupted transmission burst and recognizes, with horror, their own childhood lullaby embedded in the beacon's carrier wave. Something has been learning human language from them—and answering. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery curdling into dread.

chapters.title: What the Reactor Remembers
chapters.summary: Colony engineer Dagny Okafor's POV. During routine maintenance she finds the reactor's firmware stamped with a commissioning date that predates the colony itself, wired to receive external commands. She files a report nobody reads. Emotional beat: professional pride shaken by institutional erasure.

chapters.title: Sefa Climbs the Hill
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Following the dream-map, Sefa hikes to Ivo's relay station and asks the stranger a question no adult ever has: 'What do you talk to up there?' Ivo lies badly. Emotional beat: first fragile contact between the colony's two outcasts.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Fleet POV via intercepted comms. The Concordat and the Meridian Compact both detect the beacon's anomalous emissions and each concludes the other is testing a forbidden weapon over Terminal Anew. Both set course. Emotional beat: cold, procedural menace.

chapters.title: The Dream That Counts
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The shared dream changes: the falling star now lands, and the children wake reciting numbers none of them know. Dagny cross-references the numbers against reactor telemetry and goes pale—they're a countdown. Emotional beat: childhood wonder turning to fear.

chapters.title: Confessions at the Relay
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Cornered by Dagny and Sefa, Ivo admits everything: the signal that rewired their mind, the beacon's true function as a translator node, and that the countdown is addressed not to the colony but to whatever is coming. Emotional beat: shame transformed into reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Terminal Anew Declares Nothing
chapters.summary: Dagny's POV. The colony council refuses to evacuate or believe them; admitting the truth means admitting the colony was built atop someone else's machinery. Dagny chooses the children over the council. Emotional beat: betrayal by institutions, loyalty found sideways.

chapters.title: Lessons in Lying Beautifully
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo begins composing the plague-broadcast—a fiction in two fleet dialects, grammatically flawless, emotionally devastating. Sefa helps, because children know best how stories should hurt. Emotional beat: dark comedy and tenderness in a doomed workshop.

chapters.title: First Contact Is a Quarantine Flag
chapters.summary: Fleet POV. The Meridian advance scout reaches the system, reads Ivo's partial broadcast, and halts—but flags the data for Concordat interception. The clock accelerates. Emotional beat: hope undercut by bureaucracy.

chapters.title: The Children Stop Sleeping Alone
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The dreams deepen; the children begin finishing each other's sentences in waking hours, sharing a vocabulary that isn't human. Parents panic. Sefa defends the bond that makes her feel less alone than she ever has. Emotional beat: found family forming inside fear.

chapters.title: Sabotage in the Dark
chapters.summary: Dagny's POV. A council faction attempts to shut down the beacon to 'stop drawing attention,' nearly severing Ivo's link mid-broadcast. Dagny physically interposes herself between wrenches and wiring. Emotional beat: righteous fury.

chapters.title: What Ivo Gave Away
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, retrospective. Flashback to the original contact: how Ivo traded their human dreams for fluency in the signal, and why they've hidden here since. Understanding dawns—the beacon isn't counting down to destruction but to a question it must ask before the fleets arrive. Emotional beat: grief reconciled with purpose.

chapters.title: The Plague That Never Was
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The full broadcast goes out: casualty figures, quarantine protocols, a mother's last message composed by Sefa from real grief borrowed from her own past. Both fleets waver. One believes. Emotional beat: the terrible power of a well-told lie.

chapters.title: Concordat Breaks Formation
chapters.summary: Fleet POV. The Concordat, unconvinced, launches a reconnaissance drop. Its commander receives the beacon's true message—not a weapon, but an invitation to witness something older than either empire—and must choose between orders and awe. Emotional beat: a soldier's crisis of conscience.

chapters.title: Countdown Zero Approaches
chapters.summary: Dagny's POV. With hours left, the reactor begins venting per the alien protocol; the colony must choose: cut the power and kill the message, or let it finish and trust strangers. The council fractures; the children vote as a bloc. Emotional beat: democracy under pressure.

chapters.title: The Question Asked at Last
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At zero, the beacon speaks through Ivo entirely—a question in every language at once, including ones no human mouth should hold. The fleets hear it. The children hear it. Ivo hears themselves answer before knowing they could. Emotional beat: transcendence and terror entwined.

chapters.title: Fleets Turn Home
chapters.summary: Fleet POV. Whatever the question was, both admiralties independently log the same conclusion: nothing here belongs to anyone. The war postures dissolve; the Concordat commander burns her orders rather than file them. Emotional beat: relief so vast it feels like vertigo.

chapters.title: The Price of the Voice
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The transmission cost Ivo their remaining human language centers; they can no longer speak to the colony except through the beacon. They choose to stay aboard permanently, becoming the station's resident voice. Farewell scene with Sefa and Dagny at the airlock. Emotional beat: sacrifice without martyrdom—chosen belonging.

chapters.title: A Colony That Admits Everything
chapters.summary: Dagny's POV. The colony rewrites its charter around the truth: they are custodians, not owners. Dagny becomes liaison to the beacon, teaching children to visit Ivo legally. The council that lied is voted out gently. Emotional beat: justice achieved without vengeance.

chapters.title: Dreaming in No Language at All
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV, coda. Years later, Sefa—now a linguist herself—visits the beacon and dreams beside it. Ivo's voice greets her in a language made of two people's histories. The final line mirrors the blurb: staying invisible was never really an option, and visibility turned out to be home. Emotional beat: warm, earned peace.
